Brief Hospital Course:
** Note - this hospital course summary was completed by ___ 
___, the attending Hospiatlist responsible for Ms. ___ care 
from the time she left the ICU to the medical ward until 
discharge (only from the night of ___ until her discharge on 
___.  For details of her care prior to this point refer to 
Dr. ___ (for admission until transferred to the ICU) and 
then to Drs. ___ of the Pulmonary Division (for 
the details of her hospitalization in the ICU) - the following 
represents the summary of the care for the dates that I was her 
physician ___

In brief (initial course obtained from reading the medical chart 
for the dates prior to ___: ___ with HIV on HAART, HCV, 
bipolar disorder, and chronic pain, COPD v. Asthma initially 
presented with pyuria and fever, coughing and dyspnea; this was 
initially managed as a copd exacerbation with steroids and 
antibiotics, and at some point she became progressively more 
dyspneic and hypoxic, requiring transfer to the ICU where she 
was found to have pulmonary edema, and underwent aggressive 
diuresis for 14 litres of fluid.  She stabilized, and surface 
echo was completed to evaluate the etiology of her pulm. edema.  
Due to her obesity, echo images were of insufficient quality for 
evaluation of possible pulm htn, or shunt.   Due to this, and as 
pulm hypertension was felt to be likely either due to HIV 
disease, copd, or obstructive sleep apnea, cardiology was 
consulted in order to evaluate for the need for Rt. heart 
catheterization to eval for pulm. htn.  She was then transferred 
to me on the medical ward.  At this time cardiology had not 
given formal input re: this question.  Over a period of days, 
and in discussion with psychiatry, the patients health care 
proxy, the patient, and cardiology I managed to arrange for rt. 
heart catheterization on ___.  However, right before this was 
to be done, the pt. refused.  She did not have capacity to make 
this decision, however, as it was diagnostic, and non urgent, 
and as she would have to comply for the proceedure to be safely 
done, it was cancelled.  

She was ambulatory, afebrile, and saturating 95% on room air, so 
she was discharged home with follow up with Dr. ___ 
pulmonary arranged; she should have rt. heart cath arranged as 
an outpatient if Dr. ___ Dr. ___ PCP) agree with the 
utility of this examination given her above mentioned episode of 
pulm edema and hypoxia of unclear etiology.

INDICATION:  ___ female with dyspnea.

___.

AP UPRIGHT CHEST:  The cardiac, mediastinal and hilar contours are normal.
Linear opacity in the left mid lung, likely scar given its unchanged
appearance from the prior study.  No focal areas of consolidation are
identified to indicate pneumonia.  The pulmonary vasculature is normal.  There
is no sizeable pleural effusion or pneumothorax.  There is evidence of
surgical fixation hardware involving the  right proximal humerus.

IMPRESSION:  No pneumonia or CHF.  Stable linear opacity, likely scarring in
the left mid-lung.

HISTORY:  Shortness of breath.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT imaging was performed from the thoracic inlet through to the
hemidiaphragms before and during the intravenous administration of contrast.

FINDINGS:  There is no evidence of pulmonary embolism.  Nonpathologic
prevascular adenopathy is appreciated and unchanged compared to the exam of
___.  There is also a single right upper lobe nodule approximately 2 mm
in size, also unchanged.  These findings are consistent with mild
bronchiectasis at both lung bases, lung parenchyma is otherwise unremarkable,
as is the heart and great neck vessels.  Bony structures again demonstrate
marked vertebral compression at T6 and T9, unchanged compared to the prior
exam.  Also again appreciated is some mild dilatation of the esophagus to the
level just above the GE junction.

IMPRESSION:  No change compared to the exam of ___ and in particular, no
evidence of pulmonary embolism.  Chronic findings as described above and
unchanged.

INDICATION:  Evaluate for new infiltrate.
